policy: All five shown images were directly viewed. Illustrative observations only; no change to locked evaluations or historical exact-pixel uncertainty, no user approval.

records.observation: The two actual HTTP outputs have clearly shifted foliage and path to a brown/sepia rendering, with retained scene and visible cloud/road details. They are more desaturated and less orange than the historical reference. Historical regression illustration only.

Actual 960x640 input/output whole pixels copied without resampling. The sky is lighter, but red/green mottling and fine colour speckling are visibly more pronounced, while the bottom remains very dark. This observation illustrates the unresolved quality risk; do not replace the frozen uncertain grade or declare a new major adjudication.

Actual 768 PNG export pixels. The same exposure increases visible sky grain and color speckling; original stars remain visible. Both R22 variants refused/no result. Encoding changes do not make this an independent photo.

Actual 768 JPEG q75 export pixels. Exposure makes broad chroma variation and compression/grain patterns more visible; image remains dark in the foreground. No new quality grade or implication that all exposure strengths are impossible.

Actual 512 PNG export pixels. Exposure again makes sky grain more prominent despite a different scale; foreground stays very dark. Compare only these fixed models and this known night source, not general camera noise.
